summary: Jean-François Desgranges was an Indologist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (École normale) in 1795 and studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy.

Jean-François Jarrige was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Lycée Claude Fauriel, the École du Louvre, and the University of Paris, and served as director and head of the Guimet Museum from 1986 to around 2008.

Jean-François Lyotard was a philosopher who studied at the University of Paris and Paris Nanterre University. He held academic posts at the University of Paris, Paris Nanterre, Paris 1, Paris 8, UC Irvine, and Emory University.
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher. He studied at Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, Lycée du Parc from around 1941 to 1943, and the École Normale Supérieure in 1943.

Jean-Jacques Bochinger worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Strasbourg, Heidelberg University, and the University of Göttingen, and under Eugène Burnouf. In 1830, he served as a minister at the University of Strasbourg.

Jean-Jacques-Antoine Ampère worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Lycée Henri-IV and under Eugène Burnouf, and held posts at the Sorbonne, the École Normale Supérieure, and as Professor of Literature at the Collège de France (1833–1864).

Jean-Louis Burnouf was a linguist who studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held posts at Lycée Charlemagne, Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the École Normale Supérieure, the Collège de France (1817–1844), and as chief librarian at the University of Paris.

Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique, attested in 2003–2004.

Jean-Luc Chevillard is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli, and held posts at the CNRS around 1993 and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Jean-Marie Casal was an archaeologist who studied at the Musée du Louvre under Philippe Stern. His career included posts at the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan, Musées Nationaux, and as research director at the CNRS (1969–1975).

Jean-Noël Robert specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at INALCO under Bernard Frank, holding positions at CNRS, EPHE, the Institut des hautes études japonaises, and a professorship at the Collège de France from 2011 to 2022.

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the Chair for Chinese at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Burgundy and INALCO under Yves Hervouet, and served as President of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from around 1998 to 2004.

Jean-Pierre de Menasce was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at Balliol College, the Sorbonne, and under Émile Benveniste, later teaching at the University of Fribourg and the EPHE (1949–1970).
Jean-Pierre-Guillaume Pauthier was a scholar in sinology and Indology. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat and Antoine-Léonard Chézy between circa 1823 and 1832.
Jean-Sylvain Bailly was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the French Academy of Sciences and became a member of the Académie Française in 1763.

Jeannette M. van Gelder was an Indologist. She studied at Leiden University and Utrecht University under scholars including Willem Caland, and later held positions at Utrecht University and as a librarian at the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences.

Jeannine Auboyer was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. She studied at the École du Louvre and the EPHE under several scholars, later serving as chief curator at the Guimet Museum (1965–1980) and professor at the École du Louvre.

Jeff Dolven studied at the University of Oxford and Yale University. He held positions at Harvard University and Brandeis University, and became professor of English at Princeton University around 2001.

Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. He held posts at the University of New England, Murdoch University, and the University of Tasmania, where he became Professor in 1999.
